annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ruf, E.; Lehmann, S.; Misoch, S.
key_provisions_or_claims: Swiss survey measured public agreement with seven ethical concerns about robots for older adults.
Reduced human contact and sensitive data problems received the most agreement.
Nearly half of respondents had no concerns about job loss or privacy violation.
Deception, compromised self-determination and dignity violations received less agreement.
Further ethical considerations for future studies are discussed.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper reporting a Swiss survey of the general public's agreement with ethical concerns about using robots to support older adults and caregivers. Concerns about reduced human contact and sensitive data were strongest; job loss, privacy violation, deception, self-determination and dignity drew less agreement.
annotation.title_clean: Ethical Concerns of the General Public regarding the Use of Robots for Older Adults
annotation.title_en: Ethical Concerns of the General Public regarding the Use of Robots for Older Adults
annotation.venue: Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Information and Communication Technologies for Ageing Well and e-Health (ICT4AWE), SciTePress
